new_entities.name: Hydrolysed collagen peptides
new_entities.description: Orally consumed hydrolysed collagen peptide supplements marketed for skin, joint, and connective tissue support.

new_entities.name: Clinical skin hydration
new_entities.description: Clinically measured or instrument-measured skin hydration in human trials.

edges.effect_quant: The 2023 meta-analysis of 26 randomized trials reported a strong overall hydration signal in favor of hydrolysed collagen (Z = 4.94, p < 0.00001). Two additional meta-analyses of 14 and 19 trial sets also found hydration improved relative to placebo.
edges.population: mostly adult women with dry or photoaged skin taking oral hydrolysed collagen for several weeks to months
edges.mechanism: Collagen-derived peptides may improve dermal matrix support and water retention, which can modestly raise skin moisture measurements during supplementation.
edges.summary: The skin-hydration signal for oral hydrolysed collagen is fairly consistent across pooled randomized trials. Compared with many cosmetic-supplement claims, this one has a comparatively real evidence base, although the benefit is still modest and cosmetic rather than medical.
edges.caveats: Hydration improvements do not automatically imply wrinkle reversal or long-term structural change. The underlying trials remain heterogeneous in product formulation, duration, and sponsorship.

evidence.notes: Effects of Oral Collagen for Skin Anti-Aging: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

evidence.citation: deMirandaRB et al 2021 Int J Dermatol
evidence.notes: Effects of hydrolyzed collagen supplementation on skin aging: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Exploring the Impact of Hydrolyzed Collagen Oral Supplementation on Skin Rejuvenation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
